_doc: MEASURED inventory of the CURRENT research content, generated by tools/extract_current.py.

closureCount/closureCost: the node plus a cheapest satisfying prerequisite set (greedy over OR alternatives; an upper bound on the true minimum). depthMin: shortest prerequisite chain (roots = 1). unlockAudit: copied from docs/research-gameplay-unlock-audit.md section 5.

researchStage.requires: medicine_hippocratic AND (geometry_axiomatic OR algebra) AND stamp_seal AND legal_code_roman

rpPerTurn.input: population (military population weighted below 1 — weight is a calibration parameter, inert until soldier accounting exists)
rpPerTurn.unit: Research Points per strategic turn — scoped exception to law 3 (ADR-030); never multiplied by dt

costModel.U_basis: unit calibration: a magnitude-0 node takes a founded civilization (5,000 people, 30.8 RP/turn) 3 turns
costModel.K_basis: content scale: each magnitude point doubles cognitive effort
costModel.magnitude: novelty + difficulty + material + institutional + breadth + prerequisite complexity; Age enters only as a bounded prior inside difficulty and institutional

tuning._cityStatePaceFraction: R2a (docs/city-state-progression.md; Director decisions 4 and 12). TUNE, CHOSEN (L6): an UNCONTROLLED settlement researches autonomously with RP = cityStatePaceFraction x rpPerTurn(its own population). Reference: Civ VI city-states do not research at all; the Director rules ours progress slowly. 0.25 of the organized rate (before the sublinearity penalty of being one settlement) keeps a city-state substantially slower than a civilization of the same population. 0 disables city-state research.

nodes.name: Controlled-fire pyrotechnology
nodes.emerged: ~164 kya heat-treated silcrete (Pinnacle Point); routine by ~70 kya
nodes.costNote: founding technology of all pyrotechnology

capabilities: heat treatment of stone and wood
techniques: Heat treatment of silcrete and flint

nodes.desc: Advanced, deliberate use of controlled fire — sustained managed hearths and earth ovens, heat treatment of stone, planned landscape burning. Fire itself (making, keeping, cooking) is baseline and needs no research (D-047 ruling 2).

nodes.name: Oldowan flaking
nodes.desc: Simple hard-hammer percussion producing choppers and sharp flakes.

nodes.name: Prepared-core (Levallois)
nodes.desc: Shaping a core so a flake of predetermined form detaches — standardised points.

nodes.name: Blade production
nodes.emerged: ~40 kya Upper Palaeolithic; earlier in Africa (~70 kya)

eurekas.text: An obsidian or fine flint source is in range

nodes.desc: Long parallel-sided blades struck from prismatic cores — efficient use of raw material, many tool forms from one core.

nodes.name: Pressure flaking
nodes.costNote: a skilled refinement of knapping
nodes.desc: Removing flakes by pressing rather than striking — fine, thin, symmetrical points.

nodes.name: Heat treatment of stone

capabilities: workable stone from poor raw material

nodes.desc: Heating silcrete or chert to improve flaking — the first pyrotechnology applied to a material property.

nodes.name: Microliths and composite tools
nodes.desc: Small geometric blade segments set in series into wood or bone — replaceable cutting edges, barbed points.

nodes.name: Ground-edge axe
nodes.desc: Axes shaped by grinding rather than flaking — durable, resharpenable. Japan and Australia 25,000 years before the Neolithic.

nodes.name: Compound adhesives

capabilities: load-bearing compound adhesive for composite hafting

eurekas.text: Resin, bitumen or ochre is already gathered and worked for daily binding

nodes.desc: Engineered binders — resin loaded with ochre or beeswax, heat-processed bitumen — for load-bearing composite hafting. Simple gum, resin and sinew binding is baseline (D-047 ruling 3).

nodes.name: Birch-bark tar
nodes.desc: Dry distillation of birch bark to produce tar — a manufactured adhesive requiring controlled heating without oxygen.

nodes.name: Composite hafting
nodes.desc: Precision-fitted composite tools — shaped tang, socket or split haft bound with sinew and compound adhesive — that survive repeated impact. Simple hafted tools are baseline (D-047 ruling 3).

nodes.name: Cordage
nodes.emerged: ~50 kya Abri du Maras (direct); older inferred
nodes.desc: Twisting plant or animal fibre into string and rope.

nodes.name: Basketry
nodes.emerged: ~27 kya Pavlov impressions; ~10 kya Guitarrero Cave
nodes.desc: Woven or coiled containers from plant material — the container before pottery.

nodes.name: Spear-thrower
nodes.desc: Lever that extends the throwing arm — darts at higher velocity and range.

nodes.name: Simple bow
nodes.desc: Self bow of a single stave with a fibre string — stored-energy projectile.

nodes.name: Sling
nodes.desc: Cord pouch launching stones — cheap, deadly, a shepherd's weapon.

nodes.name: Framed hut
nodes.desc: Durable dwelling on a frame — mammoth-bone, timber post, or turf — for seasonal occupation.

nodes.name: Hide working
nodes.desc: Scraping, stretching, and softening animal skins into usable leather and fur.

nodes.name: Eyed needle and sewing
nodes.desc: Bone needles for fitted, sewn garments — cold-climate expansion enabler.

nodes.name: Sea-crossing raft

capabilities: open-water crossing beyond sight of land

nodes.desc: Large lashed log or reed rafts with steering oars, built for open-water crossings beyond sight of land. Simple riverine and shore-hugging craft are baseline (D-047 ruling 7); research unlocks the class and builds no vessel.

nodes.name: Load-carrying dugout

capabilities: lake and estuary freight by dugout

eurekas.text: Large trees grow beside navigable water

nodes.desc: Large log hollowed by fire and adze into a stable load-carrying hull. Simple log floats and small canoes for river crossing are baseline (D-047 ruling 7); research unlocks the class and builds no vessel.

nodes.name: Line and pelagic fishing
nodes.desc: Specialised hook-and-line gear — shell or bone hooks, weighted lines, lures — for deep-water and pelagic species. Basic fishing is baseline and needs no hook or node (D-047 rulings 4 and 6).

nodes.name: Grinding stone
nodes.emerged: ~30 kya Bilancino; routine in Natufian ~12 kya
nodes.desc: Quern and handstone for processing seeds, tubers, pigment.

nodes.name: Dog domestication
nodes.desc: First domesticate, from wolf, well before agriculture.

nodes.name: Pigment processing
nodes.desc: Grinding and mixing ochre for marking, adhesive additive, hide preservation.

nodes.name: Bone and antler tools
nodes.desc: Carved bone, antler, ivory — awls, points, harpoons, needles. Requires groove-and-splinter technique.

nodes.name: Oil lamp
nodes.desc: Stone lamp burning animal fat with a moss wick — light in caves.

nodes.name: Tally marks
nodes.desc: Incised counting marks on bone — Ishango, Lebombo.

nodes.name: Cereal cultivation
nodes.desc: Deliberate sowing of wild-type cereal — tending before genetic domestication. Pre-domestication cultivation lasted ~1,000 years.

nodes.name: Domesticated cereal
nodes.desc: Non-shattering rachis, larger grain — the genetic result of ~1,000 years of harvesting with sickles.

nodes.name: Wet rice cultivation

capabilities: highest yield per area of any pre-modern cereal

eurekas.text: Wild rice grows in wetlands in range

nodes.desc: Paddy cultivation of domesticated rice — flooded fields, transplanting.

nodes.name: Millet cultivation
nodes.desc: Broomcorn and foxtail millet — dry-farming cereal of the Yellow River.

nodes.name: Maize domestication
nodes.desc: From teosinte — the most genetically transformed of all crops; took millennia to become a staple.

nodes.name: African cereal domestication
nodes.desc: Sorghum and pearl millet — Sahel domesticates adapted to drought.

nodes.name: Root and tuber cultivation

capabilities: no granary needed — stored in ground

nodes.desc: Vegetative propagation — taro, yam, potato, manioc, sweet potato. Different from seed agriculture: clonal, no seed to store.

nodes.name: Legume cultivation
nodes.desc: Lentil, pea, chickpea, bean — protein and nitrogen fixation. Co-domesticated with cereals in every centre.

nodes.name: Fruit tree cultivation
nodes.desc: Olive, fig, date, grape — long-lived perennials requiring multi-decade investment and sedentism.

nodes.name: Sickle
nodes.desc: Curved harvesting blade — first microlith-set, then flint, then metal.

nodes.name: Hoe
nodes.desc: Hafted blade for tillage — the cultivation tool before the plough. Digging-stick cultivation is baseline (D-047).

nodes.name: Nixtamalization
nodes.costNote: alkaline cooking with ash or lime; no engineered material

capabilities: maize as sole staple without deficiency

eurekas.text: Wood ash or lime is used in cooking

nodes.desc: Cooking maize in alkaline solution — releases niacin, prevents pellagra. Maize as a staple depends on it.

nodes.name: Sheep and goat domestication

eurekas.text: Wild sheep or goats range nearby

nodes.desc: First herd animals — meat, later milk and wool.

nodes.name: Cattle domestication
nodes.emerged: ~8,500 BCE Near East; ~7,000 BCE Indus; possibly Sahara
nodes.desc: Taurine (Near East) and zebu (Indus) — independently. Meat, then milk, traction, dung.

nodes.name: Pig domestication
nodes.desc: From wild boar — independently in Near East and China. Omnivore; village scavenger.

nodes.name: Milking and dairying
nodes.desc: Exploiting living animals for milk — requires either lactase persistence or processing into cheese/yogurt.

nodes.name: Wool sheep and fleece
nodes.desc: Selection for fleece-bearing sheep — wool as a fibre.

nodes.name: Animal traction
nodes.desc: Yoking cattle to pull — the prerequisite for plough and cart.

nodes.name: Open-fired pottery
nodes.emerged: ~18,000 BCE Xianrendong; ~14,000 BCE Jomon; ~9,000 BCE Near East; ~9,400 BCE Mali
nodes.desc: Coil-built vessels fired in a bonfire — low temperature, porous, but a container that boils.

nodes.name: Updraft kiln
nodes.desc: Enclosed firing chamber with a firebox below — >900°C, controlled atmosphere. The thermal precondition for smelting.

nodes.name: Fast wheel (throwing)
nodes.desc: Flywheel-momentum wheel permitting thrown pottery — mass production, a specialist craft.

nodes.name: Mudbrick
nodes.desc: Sun-dried clay bricks — modular, repairable, multi-storey.

nodes.name: Lime plaster
nodes.desc: Burning limestone to quicklime, slaking, applying — floors, walls, and the first chemically transformed building material.

nodes.name: Timber-frame construction
nodes.desc: Post-and-beam structures — longhouses of the LBK, pile dwellings.

nodes.name: Dry-stone construction
nodes.emerged: ~10,000 BCE Göbekli Tepe; ~3,000 BCE Skara Brae
nodes.desc: Walls and structures of fitted unmortared stone.

nodes.name: Dug well
nodes.desc: Excavated shaft to groundwater — settlement independent of surface water.

nodes.name: Grain fermentation (beer)
nodes.desc: Malting and brewing — grain into a storable, nutritious, safe drink.

nodes.name: Wine and fruit fermentation
nodes.desc: Fermenting grape, honey, fruit.

nodes.name: Oil pressing
nodes.desc: Extracting olive, sesame, flax oil by crushing and pressing.

nodes.name: Salt production

eurekas.text: Brine springs, salt pans or a sea coast

nodes.desc: Evaporating brine or mining rock salt — the preservative and the trade good.

nodes.name: Flax cultivation
nodes.emerged: ~8,000 BCE Levant (wild flax use ~30 kya Dzudzuana)
nodes.desc: Growing flax for linen fibre and oil.

nodes.name: Spindle spinning
nodes.desc: Drop spindle with whorl — continuous thread from fibre.

nodes.name: Warp-weighted loom
nodes.desc: Vertical loom with weighted warps — wide cloth, complex weaves.

unlockAudit.consequences:

`inst.textile_workshop` → no realizing system

nodes.name: Dyeing
nodes.desc: Colouring fibre with plant and mineral dyes — madder, woad, indigo, with mordants.

nodes.name: Native copper working
nodes.desc: Cold-hammering and annealing metallic copper nuggets — beads, awls. Not smelting.

nodes.name: Copper smelting
nodes.desc: Reducing malachite/azurite to metal in a charcoal fire — the first extractive metallurgy.

nodes.name: Charcoal making
nodes.desc: Pyrolysing wood in a covered pile — a fuel hot enough for metallurgy.

nodes.name: Open-mould casting
nodes.desc: Pouring molten copper into a one-piece stone mould — axes, blades.

nodes.name: Native gold and silver
nodes.desc: Working native gold and silver — ornament, then value store.

nodes.name: Basin irrigation
nodes.desc: Trapping floodwater in bunded basins — Nile and Indus mode.

nodes.name: Canal irrigation

eurekas.text: An arid floodplain watered by a river

nodes.desc: Diverting river water through dug channels — Mesopotamian mode. Requires levelling and maintenance.

nodes.name: Agricultural terracing
nodes.desc: Stepped fields on slopes — soil retention, water control, arable from hillside.

nodes.name: Sledge
nodes.desc: Runners for hauling loads over snow, mud, or grass — the vehicle before the wheel.

nodes.name: Solid wheel and axle
nodes.desc: Disc wheel on a fixed or rotating axle — from the potter's wheel principle to the vehicle.

nodes.name: Ox cart

capabilities: bulk overland transport at cart range

nodes.desc: Two-wheeled cart drawn by oxen — bulk haulage overland.

nodes.name: Trackway

capabilities: trackway infrastructure class (path tier: timber causeway and stoned track)

nodes.desc: Trackway — an IMPROVED PATH, not an engineered road: timber causeway and corduroy across marsh, cleared and stoned track (Sweet Track). An infrastructure-class unlock (path tier): road development builds the trackways, and basic dirt paths are baseline (D-047 ruling 8; ADR-032). The engineered built road additionally needs dry-stone construction (infra.road_built requires track_road AND stone_dry).

nodes.name: Ard plough
nodes.emerged: ~4,000 BCE (plough marks under barrows; Uruk pictograph)
nodes.desc: Animal-drawn scratch plough — multiplies cultivable area per farmer.

nodes.name: Clay tokens
nodes.desc: Geometric clay counters for commodities — one token per unit.

nodes.name: Stamp seal
nodes.desc: Carved stone impressed in clay — ownership, authentication.

nodes.name: Lunar calendar
nodes.desc: Tracking months by moon phases — sowing and festival timing.

nodes.name: Trepanation
nodes.costNote: skilled stone-tool surgery
nodes.desc: Surgical opening of the skull — with survival rates over 50%.

nodes.name: Arsenical bronze

capabilities: harder tools and weapons without tin trade

eurekas.text: Arsenic-bearing copper ores (fahlore, enargite, arsenopyrite-rich deposits) are smelted locally

nodes.desc: Copper smelted from arsenic-bearing ores — harder than copper, castable, and NEEDS NO TIN. Most early "bronze" was this.

nodes.name: Tin bronze

eurekas.text: Tin ore is held, locally or by trade

nodes.desc: Copper alloyed with ~10% tin — superior, reproducible, but tin sources are rare and distant.

nodes.name: Two-piece and closed-mould casting
nodes.desc: Bivalve moulds for symmetrical objects — socketed axes, spearheads.

nodes.name: Lost-wax casting
nodes.desc: Wax model, clay investment, wax melted out, metal poured — any shape, one use.

nodes.name: Sheet metalwork
nodes.desc: Hammering bronze into sheet — vessels, helmets, armour by raising and chasing.

nodes.name: Shaft mining
nodes.desc: Vertical shafts and galleries following ore — Grimes Graves flint, Timna copper, Great Orme.

nodes.name: Proto-cuneiform
nodes.desc: Pictographic accounting tablets — commodity + number, no syntax.

nodes.name: Cuneiform (full writing)
nodes.desc: Phonetic signs, syntax — language on clay. Sumerian, then Akkadian, Hittite, Elamite.

nodes.name: Papyrus
nodes.desc: Writing surface from pith strips — light, portable, and the first document technology.

nodes.name: Sexagesimal place-value
nodes.desc: Base-60 positional notation — the first place-value system.

nodes.name: Babylonian arithmetic
nodes.desc: Reciprocal tables, squares, quadratic problems — computational mathematics.

nodes.name: Land surveying
nodes.desc: Measuring and recording field boundaries — rope-stretchers, the 3-4-5 triangle.

nodes.name: Square sail
nodes.emerged: ~3,500 BCE Naqada II depictions; ~5,000 BCE Kuwait (possible)

capabilities: improved coastal and seagoing transport class (sail)
upriver travel under sail instead of rowing
river and coastal trade at scale under sail

eurekas.text: A navigable river or sheltered coast with steady winds

nodes.desc: Wind propulsion — first on the Nile. Unlocks the improved coastal and seagoing transport class (D-047 ruling 7); primitive river and shore-hugging craft are baseline, and the realizing systems build the vessels.

nodes.name: Plank-built boat
nodes.desc: Hull from sewn or pegged planks — larger than a log allows.

nodes.name: Horse domestication
nodes.desc: On the Pontic-Caspian steppe; DOM2 lineage spreads ~2,200 BCE.

nodes.name: Donkey domestication
nodes.desc: From African wild ass — the pack animal of the ancient Near East and Africa.

nodes.name: Camel domestication

eurekas.text: Wild camels range in arid zones

nodes.desc: Dromedary (Arabia) and Bactrian (Central Asia) — desert and steppe transport.

nodes.name: Spoked wheel
nodes.desc: Light wheel with spokes — requires bent-wood or joined felloes, precise hub.

nodes.name: Chariot
nodes.desc: Light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle — the dominant military platform of the Late Bronze Age.

nodes.name: Composite bow
nodes.desc: Laminated horn, wood, sinew — short, powerful, suited to horseback.

nodes.name: Fired brick
nodes.desc: Kiln-fired bricks — waterproof, durable, standardised.

unlockAudit.consequences:

nodes.name: Glaze and faience

eurekas.text: Natron or plant-ash alkali is already used in washing, embalming or ceramic work

nodes.desc: Vitreous coatings and quartz-paste objects — the road to glass.

nodes.name: Core-formed glass

eurekas.text: Natron or plant ash is available

nodes.desc: Glass vessels formed around a removable core — the first glassware.

nodes.name: Standardised weights
nodes.desc: State-issued weight standards — Indus cubical weights, Mesopotamian mina/shekel.

nodes.name: Civil solar calendar
nodes.prereq: calendar_lunar AND (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script)
nodes.desc: 365-day administrative year decoupled from lunar months — Egypt.

nodes.name: Water clock
nodes.desc: Clepsydra — measuring time by regulated flow.

nodes.name: Medical texts
nodes.desc: Written prescriptions and case descriptions — Edwin Smith papyrus, Sumerian pharmacopoeia.

nodes.name: Beekeeping
nodes.emerged: ~2,400 BCE Egypt; ~900 BCE Tel Rehov apiary

eurekas.text: Wild honeybees nest in the region

nodes.desc: Managed hives — honey (the only concentrated sweetener) and wax (for lost-wax casting).

nodes.name: Bloomery iron
nodes.emerged: ~1,800 BCE Anatolia; ~1,200 BCE widespread; ~1,000 BCE Sub-Saharan; ~1,200 BCE India
nodes.desc: Reducing iron ore to a spongy bloom below melting point, then consolidating by hammering. Ore is everywhere; tin is not.

nodes.name: Bellows
nodes.desc: Forced draught — leather bag or piston — raising furnace temperature.

nodes.name: Carburized steel
nodes.desc: Prolonged heating of wrought iron in charcoal, absorbing carbon — hardened edges.

nodes.name: Quench hardening
nodes.desc: Rapid cooling of carburized steel — martensite. Brittle unless tempered.

nodes.name: Tempering
nodes.desc: Reheating quenched steel to reduce brittleness — the full heat-treatment cycle.

nodes.name: Wootz crucible steel
nodes.desc: Iron and carbon fused in a sealed crucible — homogeneous high-carbon steel. India, ~500 BCE. The Damascus blade source.

nodes.name: Pattern welding
nodes.desc: Forge-welding strips of iron and steel — combining toughness and hardness in one blade.

nodes.name: Consonantal alphabet

capabilities: commercial records without a scribal class

nodes.desc: ~22 signs, one per consonant — Proto-Sinaitic to Phoenician. Learnable in weeks.

nodes.name: Brahmi script
nodes.desc: Indian alphasyllabary — ancestor of all Indic scripts. Independent or Aramaic-derived (debated).

nodes.name: Weighed silver
nodes.desc: Silver by weight as medium of exchange — cut pieces, standard weights. Money before coins.

eurekas.text: Electrum (natural gold–silver alloy) occurs in range

nodes.name: Cavalry
nodes.desc: Fighting from horseback — replaces the chariot everywhere within 300 years.

nodes.name: Saddle
nodes.desc: Padded seat — rider stability before the stirrup.

capabilities: the tax edict: a declared levy on the realm's production
tribute in kind assessed on the harvest
obligations recorded and owed to the state
techniques: Levy in kind into sealed stores

nodes.desc: Taxation: the levy of tribute in kind — a counted share of the harvest, herd or craft output owed to the ruler or temple, assessed against the harvest and delivered into sealed stores. Its evidence is the Uruk and Ur III grain-receipt tablets, the sealed storerooms of the Ubaid and Uruk temples, and the Egyptian harvest assessment recorded beside the Nile gauge. A community without a record of what is owed has gifts and feasting, not a levy, so no Stone Age society taxes. Researching it gives the polity the knowledge of the tax edict (SetTaxRate); the edict is operational only once the polity has entered Age III, the Bronze Age (sim.json governance.taxationMinAge). Related refinements, which no longer gate the edict: tax assessment by computation (arithmetic_babylonian), taxation by area (surveying), by weight (standard_weights) and in coin (coinage_electrum). Placement: Civ VI has no tax technology — governments and their policies come through civics, starting with the first civic, Code of Laws (Chiefdom); here the causal prerequisites are counted obligations (clay tokens), sealed stores under administrative control (stamp seal) and an administrative record beyond memory (proto-cuneiform, hieroglyphic or Chinese script).

baseline.name: Settlement founding
baseline.providedBy: ColonizationSystem — a colony is founded when famine-flight migrants have no viable settlement to move to (MigrationSystem demand), or by a Found Settlement order (OrderKind 9, D-051 §5, ADR-036) from a settlement the issuer controls to an unclaimed, reachable site; founding is instantaneous — no settler unit exists

baseline.name: Scouting and exploration
baseline.providedBy: not yet simulated — no mobile agents exist (D-043)

baseline.name: Basic military (clubmen or equivalent)
baseline.providedBy: not yet simulated — the battle layer is a later milestone (D-011)

baseline.name: Basic food and resource gathering
baseline.providedBy: ProductionSystem — the Farming, Herding/fishing and Extraction sectors produce food and goods with no research (HarvestWeatherSystem supplies only the harvest multiplier); no sector is gated: research changes the ACTIVITY a sector expresses (activity.farming, .herding, .logging, .mining; sectorActivities) (ADR-033 D1); one exception changes output: with farming.preCultivation on (sim.json), the Farming sector harvests wild food at the forager rates until activity.farming is eligible for the settlement, and the cultivated yield applies once it is (R2a)

baseline.name: Basic internal construction
baseline.providedBy: ConstructionSystem — an EnqueueConstruction order queues a project; the first project in a settlement's queue is built a little each turn, as far as its materials and builders allow, and is complete when all its materials and work have gone in (what has gone in is kept while it waits and lost only if it is cancelled; D-054); no Builder unit

baseline.name: Migration and resettlement
baseline.providedBy: MigrationSystem — people move between settlements with no research

baseline.name: Fire: making, keeping and cooking
baseline.providedBy: not separately simulated — fire is known before the simulation begins (D-047 ruling 2); no node gates it, and fire_making is advanced controlled-fire use

baseline.name: Primitive tools and simple hafting
baseline.providedBy: not separately simulated — the tools good comes from crafting recipes that read no research; simple hafting and binding need no node (D-047 ruling 3), composite hafting is technology-owned

baseline.name: Basic fishing (shore, net, trap and spear)
baseline.providedBy: ProductionSystem — the Herding/fishing sector produces food from turn 1 with no research; activity.fishing requires no node (D-047 rulings 4-6), fish weirs and line/pelagic fishing are technology-owned

baseline.name: Primitive riverine and shore-hugging craft
baseline.providedBy: not yet simulated as vessels — no vessel, port or sea route exists; river movement is priced from founding by the TraversalLattice river-corridor coefficient, which reads no research (D-047 ruling 7)

baseline.name: Basic shelter
baseline.providedBy: HousingSystem — dwellings are endowed at founding and built and maintained with no research and no order

baseline.name: Basic paths and overland movement
baseline.providedBy: PathBuildSystem — dirt paths (the DirtPath edge type) accrue from use with no research and no order (D-047 ruling 8)

baseline.name: Hunting
baseline.providedBy: ProductionSystem — SIMULATED as the Herding/fishing sector's yield from wild-animal (livestock) deposits: the sector's labour turns each settlement's livestock deposit into livestock with no research. No separate hunting sector, prey population or hunting mechanism exists (the Director lists hunting as baseline, integration directive 2026-10-02; ADR-033 D1)
